thread:
marta: Heads up — p99 token latency jumped on `small-chat/v1` after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. Not across all routes, mostly short sequences.
jonah: Saw the alert. I pulled a couple of traces, KV hit rate dropped significantly for those requests. Flamegraph attached in perf-bot link.
samir: Interesting — batching heuristics were adjusted in the same change. Could be more single-sample kernel dispatches causing overhead and worse KV locality.
kai: Can someone paste the perf summary? I can't access the dashboard from my laptop right now.
perf-bot: Automated profile report: https://internal.redwood/perf/report/tr_abc123 — summary: +12ms median kernel_dispatch, KV cache miss rate 18% -> 44% on small-chat, batching mean size down 2.1 -> 1.3. Top symbols: kernel_select(), kv_lookup(), rpc_deser().
jonah: Quick snippet from trace metadata: ``trace_id=tr_abc123 route=small-chat seq_len=8 batch_size=1 kernel=fast_fp16``. You can see token-level spans for decode -> kv_lookup -> kernel -> postprocess.
kai: We need token-level latency slices on the dashboards: decode, kv-lookup, kernel_exec, postproc. Without those it's hard to correlate metric spikes to KV vs kernel.
elaine: Agreed. Also let's make sure request metrics include the trace_id tag so we can jump from a metric spike to the exact trace (and vice versa). Example metric label: `token_latency_ms{route=\"small-chat\",trace_id=\"tr_abc123\"}`.
marta: Proposed short plan: 1) revert kernel-selection heuristic to previous behavior in canary (samir), 2) add trace_id label to top-level request and token spans (kai), 3) add token-slice panels & per-route KPIs in console (jonah).
samir: I'll push the canary revert to dedicated-canary cluster now with a forced batcher config: ``batcher.min_batch=2 batcher.max_wait_ms=8`` to avoid single-sample dispatching. Rolling this to 5% first.
jonah: I'll build two dashboard panels: per-route token-slice p50/p95/p99 and per-request breakdown that surfaces the trace_id as a clickable link to traces.
kai: For tracing changes, we just need to attach the request id as `trace_id` to the root span and emit the same id as a metric label on the request_summary metric. I'll file a tiny spec and ping infra for retention change.
elaine: Also add a KPI for KV hit rate per-route. If KV hit drops when batch size shrinks that's a clear signal.
marta: Quick experiment idea: run replay on a copy of recent small-chat traffic with the new kernel vs old kernel and compare token-slice distributions. Jonah/samir can coordinate.
perf-bot: Benchmark snapshot (replay): old-kernel median_token_ms=5.4 kernel_ms=2.1 kv_ms=1.8 batch_size=2.2 | new-kernel median_token_ms=6.9 kernel_ms=3.6 kv_ms=2.5 batch_size=1.3
samir: Reverting in canary now. I'll report back with metrics in ~15m. If we see improvement, we keep revert, then iterate on kernel selection logic to prefer coalesced batches for short-seq workloads.
jonah: I'll start the dashboard PR and link to it here when ready. Also adding a per-route alert when token-level kernel_ms increases by >20% sustained for 10m.
marta: Thanks everyone. Owners: samir (canary revert), kai (trace_id + metric labels), jonah (dashboards + alerts), elaine (KV hit KPI). Follow up in this thread with short status updates. :thumbsup:
